item.title: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
Timer Expired. Edits made as discussed below. Author may revert at any time.

The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 7 days if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. If you have questions not directly related to the article about this project, please pm a member of the WikiWalk Team

+ Show Block
- Hide Block

If ever there was a place in this article that could hold a crosslink, it would be in the table where the various outputs of the factory are listed. After talking to Roget, we agreed that the metal slag entry could be changed to metal scrap the matches the metal alloy composition of other SCPs. For this purpose, I decided to roll with the metal plating of SCP-2406 and the metalic blocks of SCP-1139 As such, I am proposing the following edits:

Changing this:
Manufacturing Port λ Badly damaged, produces a constant stream of metal slag.
To this:
Manufacturing Port λ Badly damaged, produces a constant stream of metal scrap. Scrap composition varies with samples ranging from bronze alloys matching the plating of SCP-2406 to gray metals matching the blocks forming SCP-1139.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.content:encoded:
I like the notion that this is an elaborate Trojan horse. Give the Foundation a bunch of weird garbage that will hold their attention while you feed them so much high quality steel that they ultimately NEED to use it. It might take 15 or 20 years of containment before they bend the rules, using steel of anomalous provenance. Now with another 30 or 40 years and the Foundation is logistically and structurally dependent on all that "completely mundane" steel.

It reminds me of a trick from a tabletop fantasy RPG, using a variation on the classic "Wall of Iron" spell.
1. Conjure a huge wall of iron, melt it into ingots, saving a tiny piece for yourself. Repeat as often as possible.
2. Through 3rd parties, sell the ingots cheap to your enemies armies over a period of years. Hopefully, much of the enemy's weapons, armor, and tools will be made of, or adulterated with, your steel.
3. As you invade, take all of those pieces from the walls you conjured, and disenchant/dispel them, vanishing all of the metal from all of those walls.
4. Enjoy a really mean-spirited victory.

What could be wrong with the metal? ANYTHING. Maybe it listens. Maybe it has very slow side effects from exposure. Maybe it's [redacted]-permeable. Maybe it kicks pufferkittens when you're not looking…

I wish there was more here. The dash of characterization is good, but for me it's not enough.

You would throw us a bone as far as the purpose of the facility, or at least send us on a goose chase.

I like this suggestion. Either one. Like, maybe the Foundation has followed up multiple leads only to end in more confusion & weirdness. Maybe some (interesting but not quite comprehensible) changes have happened. Anything to get the fridge logic going.

As it stands it's just another crazy broken thing (which isn't bad) and it's not all that much more interesting than the other crazy broken things on the site (which is).

What makes this different? I can't see what.

Oh well.

The writing on this is, mechanically, a bit clumsy, and the conversations with the overseer are perfunctory and abrupt in a bad way. "Due to 744's immobility" puts a bee directly into my bonnet for tonal reasons. Having said that, the underlying idea is a solid one, and while I'm not sure if it's intentional or not the notion that the overseer himself doesn't know "the purpose" is kind of poignant, and makes it all a decent commentary on industrialization.

No vote, but if it's tooled up a bit I'd be pleased with this one.
